title: TryFrom Interface
concept: TryFrom defines fallible type conversions that return Result — perfect for parsing, validation, and any conversion that might fail.
why: Not all conversions succeed. Parse "abc" as Int? Fail. Validate an email? Might fail. TryFrom makes failure explicit and safe.
tips: Use TryFrom for any conversion that can fail — parsing, validation, network requests
Define a domain-specific Error type per conversion — makes error handling precise
TryFrom + `?` creates elegant validation pipelines — chain conversions together
Never implement TryFrom for conversions that should never fail — use From instead
common_mistakes: Using From for fallible conversions — callers assume From always succeeds
Returning vague error types like Str — define an enum for specific error cases
Forgetting to implement TryInto — it's auto-derived from TryFrom (like Into from From)
